html:
SMTO-LLM-0030 — The model service refused SMTO's request

GUID: 31e54be6-7e7b-493c-b0a6-a8a84a8a56d4
Slug: provider-request-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model service turned the request down without a reason SMTO recognizes. The model didn't answer, and no action ran for this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs your model service. Ask what the service's log says about the refused request at that time. The service's own log names the exact reason; SMTO only received a refusal it couldn't sort into a known cause.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. If this small test request passes, the problem is specific to this task's request rather than the whole connection.
  3. If you recently changed settings in the card's Generation section, set Profile back to Provider Defaults, select Save Main, and start a new task. A model setting the service doesn't support can cause a refusal, and new tasks pick up the saved settings.

What success looks like

  • A new task gets past its first model step without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages your model service. Don't change unrelated time limits or turn off security checks; they won't make the service accept the request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider rejected the request with a status or error text that matched no narrower classifier (not authentication, access, quota, missing model, server error or a recognised setup rejection), so it was recorded as provider_request_rejected; the specific rejected feature is unknown.

What this means

  • A provider rejection was received, but its retained category does not identify the rejected feature. The status and request phase can distinguish access, route, request-shape or service problems. Changing an unrelated timeout cannot repair an explicit rejection.

Why this can happen

  • The endpoint returned a rejection not explained by a more specific registered diagnostic.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the recorded HTTP status and validation phase. Ask the provider operator to identify the rejected field or service condition using its logs.

How to fix it

  • Use http_status in the error details and the provider's server log for the same time to find what was rejected (request size, a parameter, the route or a policy). Change only the setting or request feature the provider names, for example the role's Generation parameters in Settings › Setup › Model routing; changing unrelated timeouts will not repair an explicit rejection.
  • Use the recorded status and request phase to investigate with the provider operator. Change only the setting or request feature shown to be rejected.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts the corrected request and returns a complete supported response.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The provider rejected the request and no supported narrower classifier matched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
